subject.title: Handle mid-turn precheck compaction end to end

question: Should agent-core expose or recognize a generic control-flow-error contract for this recovery path, or should `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` remain entirely recognized within the OpenClaw-owned runner boundary?
rationale: Choosing the permanent owner and representation of a cross-package lifecycle control-flow signal is an API/architecture decision; the branch’s literal matching is not a safe default contract.

options.title: Adopt a generic marker
options.body: Have the thrower mark the control-flow error through a generic agent-core mechanism and let lifecycle code rethrow only marked errors.

options.title: Keep recognition in OpenClaw
options.body: Remove the generic agent-core and harness special cases, then handle this signal only in the OpenClaw runner that owns mid-turn recovery.

recommendation.title: Adopt a generic marker
recommendation.body: Have the thrower mark the control-flow error through a generic agent-core mechanism and let lifecycle code rethrow only marked errors.

likelyOwner.reason: Their related proposal directly explored a generic sentinel for this same lifecycle distinction.
